title: Challenge: Changing String Casing Solution
summary: Walks through the capitalise-the-first-letter challenge by decomposing it into small steps, checking each variable in the console, then adding one more step so odd input like angELA still comes out correctly.

concepts.heading: Problem decomposition
points: The main goal is a skill rather than the code: split a large problem into pieces, and split any piece that still feels hard.
Top-level plan: (1) store the prompted name, (2) capitalise its first letter, (3) greet the user in an alert.
Step 2 turned out to be too big and was split into: isolate first character, uppercase it, isolate the remainder, join them.
(Extra) Simpler one-liners exist on Stack Overflow, but the exercise deliberately restricts you to the module's tools.

concepts.heading: Verifying each step in the console
points: Run each line in the browser console as it is written and then type the variable name to confirm its value (for example the first character is a lowercase a).
This incremental checking catches mistakes early instead of debugging a finished block.

concepts.heading: Slicing the first character and the rest
points: name.slice(0, 1) starts at position 0 and stops before position 1, giving just the first character.
name.slice(1, name.length) starts after the first character and runs to the end.
Hard-coding an end index (such as 6 for Angela) only works for names of that exact length, so use the length property, which adapts to whatever the user enters.
Uppercase the isolated first character with .toUpperCase() (parentheses required) and join with + concatenation.

concepts.heading: Edge case: capital letters later in the name
points: Input like a lowercase start with capitals near the end (e.g. angELA) leaves the tail in capitals with the first version of the solution.
Fix by adding a step that reassigns the remainder: restOfName = restOfName.toLowerCase();
Lesson: test with unusual input, because real users will supply it.

task.name: Solution walkthrough: capitalised greeting
task.starting_point: Empty script; the challenge from the previous lecture.
task.goal: Greet the user with a name whose first letter is uppercase and whose other letters are lowercase.
steps: Reassign restOfName to its toLowerCase() version.
Concatenate upperCaseFirstChar + restOfName and use it in alert("Hello, " + ...).
task.expected_result: Typing angELA (or any casing) produces an alert saying Hello, Angela.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 14 - Introduction to Javascript ES6/14.08 - Challenge - Changing Casing in Text

pitfalls: Hard-coding the slice end index instead of using name.length.
Not lowercasing the remainder, so mixed-case input keeps stray capitals.
Forgetting the empty parentheses on the case methods.
(Extra) Cancelling the prompt returns null, and null.slice throws an error; the lecture does not handle this.

playground.coverage: Solution block uses slice(0,1) and slice(1) with both case methods, plus a chained one-liner and a capitalise-every-word bonus.
gaps_and_ideas: The playground solution uses slice(1) and skips the name.length reasoning; add a note on why the second argument is optional and how length was the lecture's approach.
Add the decomposition lesson explicitly: list the a to e sub-steps as a checklist in the tasks.
Add an edge-case task: test with angELA and with an empty string.
Explore demo idea: a stepper that shows the value of each intermediate variable as the learner types.
